name: GSTSetu – GST Invoices for WooCommerce
author: Wasim Akram

sections.description:
GSTSetu brings Indian GST compliance to WooCommerce stores without any external service. Everything runs inside your WordPress install: validation, numbering, tax computation and the PDF invoice itself.

GSTIN validation with checksum. Every GSTIN entered on the settings page or at checkout is normalized and checked against the official 15-character structure, the in-force state codes and the mod-36 checksum, so wrong numbers are caught before they reach an invoice.

Rule 46 invoice numbering. Invoice numbers are allocated per financial year (April 1 – March 31) and series, run consecutively and are never reused, exactly as Rule 46 of the CGST Rules expects. The counter lives in its own database table and allocation uses a row lock, so two orders paid at the same moment can never receive the same number. When a financial year rolls over in April, numbering restarts from 1 automatically.

CGST / SGST / UTGST / IGST tax engine. The plugin compares the seller’s state with the buyer’s place of supply: same state splits tax into CGST + SGST (or CGST + UTGST for union territories without a legislature), a different state charges IGST. Union territories without a legislature — Chandigarh, Lakshadweep, Ladakh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu — are handled by name.

GST 2.0 slabs. Product rates use the current four-slab structure: 0% for essentials, 5% for standard goods, 18% for standard services and goods, and 40% for sin and luxury goods. A default slab covers products without an explicit rate.

GST tax invoice PDF. Invoices are rendered with the bundled DOMPDF library (no composer, no shell access required) and stored in uploads/dwgst-invoices/ with directory listing disabled. The invoice carries every Rule 46 mandatory field: seller identity and GSTIN, consecutive serial number, issue date, buyer details and GSTIN, HSN codes, quantities, taxable values, per-tax amounts, place of supply, reverse-charge status and signature block.

Audit log. Activation, settings changes, invoice issuance, regeneration, cancellation and numbering failures are recorded with user, IP and timestamp under WooCommerce > GST Audit Log.

Email PDF delivery. The invoice PDF is attached to the customer’s order emails (processing, completed, customer invoice) and optionally to the admin new-order email, each with its own switch. Missing PDF files are regenerated on the fly without burning a new invoice number.

Customer self-service. When enabled, customers get a “GST Invoice (PDF)” download button on the My Account orders list and on the order view page. The download endpoint checks that the logged-in customer owns the order.

Credit notes (Section 34, CGST Act). When a refund is processed against an invoiced order, a GST credit note is issued automatically from its own FY series (CN/{FY}/{number}). The credit note references the original invoice number and date, states the reason, and reverses the taxable value, CGST, SGST/UTGST, IGST and CESS proportionally — capped so the cumulative credit never exceeds the invoiced value. Credit note PDFs are generated with the same DOMPDF engine and listed in the order’s GST metabox. Partial refunds get one credit note per refund.

E-invoicing (IRN). B2B invoices are eligible for e-invoicing: the plugin builds the standard NIC e-invoice payload (TranDtls, DocDtls, SellerDtls, BuyerDtls, ItemList, ValDtls), requests the IRN from the configured IRP (NIC v1.03 endpoints, sandbox or production) or runs in local mock mode for testing, and stores the IRN, acknowledgement number/date and signed QR payload. The IRN and QR code are printed on the invoice PDF, and IRNs can be generated manually or automatically per invoice with cancellation support.

GST reports. WooCommerce > GST Reports builds GSTR-1 style data from issued invoices and credit notes — B2B, B2CL, B2CS, CDNR and HSN summary — exportable as the GSTR-1 JSON (all sections) or per-section CSV files, plus a GSTR-3B outward-supply summary (intra-state, inter-state, nil-rated) as CSV.

GST dashboard. WooCommerce > GST Dashboard shows monthly tax collection cards, a month-by-month FY table, a slab-wise (rate-wise) breakdown net of credit notes, active IRN counts and credited-back totals.

GSTSetu is developed and maintained by Wasim Akram (https://www.digitalwasim.com). Setup guide and support: https://www.digitalwasim.com/blog/gstsetu-woocommerce-gst-guide or email support@digitalwasim.com.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the digitalwasim-gst-invoices-for-woocommerce folder to wp-content/plugins/ (or install the zip via Plugins > Add New > Upload).
  2. Activate the plugin. The database tables are created automatically.
  3. Open WooCommerce > GSTSetu and fill in your business details, GSTIN and numbering format.
  4. Set an HSN code and GST slab on each product under Product data > GST (India).
  5. Place a test order; the invoice is generated when the order reaches the status selected under Invoicing.
sections.faq:
Who develops this plugin?

GSTSetu is developed and maintained by Wasim Akram — https://www.digitalwasim.com. The complete setup guide and support articles live at https://www.digitalwasim.com/blog/gstsetu-woocommerce-gst-guide. For direct support, email support@digitalwasim.com. If the plugin saves you time, you can buy the developer a coffee at https://www.buymeacoffee.com/wasimb.

What is Rule 46 numbering?

Rule 46 of the CGST Rules requires tax invoices to carry a consecutive serial number, unique for the financial year, not exceeding sixteen characters. This plugin allocates numbers per FY and series with a database row lock and never reuses a number, even after cancellation or regeneration.

Does it support HPOS (high-performance order storage)?

Yes. The plugin uses WooCommerce CRUD everywhere and declares custom order tables compatibility.

Where are the PDFs stored?

In wp-content/uploads/dwgst-invoices/ with an .htaccess file blocking direct listing. Downloads go through a capability-checked admin endpoint.

Can I regenerate an invoice?

Yes — from the order screen. Regeneration keeps the original invoice number; cancellation marks the row cancelled and the number is never issued again.

How are refunds handled?

Every refund against an invoiced order automatically gets a GST credit note from its own series. The reversal amounts are proportional to the refunded amount and are capped at the invoiced total. Credit notes are listed in the GST metabox on the order screen with their PDFs.

What are the GST 2.0 slabs?

0% (essentials), 5% (standard), 18% (standard) and 40% (sin and luxury goods). You choose the slab per product; untagged products fall back to the default slab on the settings page.

Does e-invoicing work out of the box?

It runs in local mock mode by default so you can test the full flow without government credentials. For real filing, switch the environment to sandbox or production under WooCommerce > GSTSetu > E-invoicing and enter your IRP credentials.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Rebrand: the plugin is now “GSTSetu – GST Invoices for WooCommerce” (same features, same developer). Admin menu and labels renamed.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: GSTIN checksum validation, Rule 46 invoice numbering, CGST/SGST/UTGST/IGST engine with GST 2.0 slabs, HSN product fields, checkout GSTIN field, DOMPDF GST tax invoice with QR code, email PDF delivery, My Account customer downloads, Section 34 credit notes, e-invoicing (IRN) with mock/sandbox/production IRPs, GSTR-1 / GSTR-3B report exports and GST dashboard.
